import data.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Wrap a loader/action return value to attach a status code or headers.

data().description:
**Framework / Data mode.** Return data together with a status code or headers, without turning it into a `Response`.
The value still arrives at the component as a plain object.
Replaces the deprecated `json()` — return a bare object when you need no status or headers.

data() with headers.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Attach response headers to loader or action data.

import redirect.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Redirect helper for loaders and actions.

redirect().description:
**Framework / Data mode.** Redirect from a loader or action. Returns a 302 `Response`.
Inside a loader, `throw redirect(...)` is the more common form — it stops execution immediately.

throw redirect().description: **Framework / Data mode.** Abort the current loader/action and redirect. Preferred inside guard clauses, since it needs no early-return plumbing.

redirect() with status.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Redirect with an explicit status. Use 301/308 for permanent moves, 303 after a successful mutation.

import replace.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Redirect that replaces the current history entry.

replace().description:
**Framework / Data mode.** Like `redirect()`, but replaces the current history entry instead of pushing a new one.
Use it so the Back button does not return to the page that redirected.

import redirectDocument.description: **Framework / Data mode.** Redirect with a full document reload.

redirectDocument().description:
**Framework / Data mode.** Redirect with a full browser navigation instead of a client-side transition.
Use it when leaving the SPA — for example to a server-rendered auth flow on another origin.

import isRouteErrorResponse.description: Type guard separating thrown `Response`s from real errors.

isRouteErrorResponse().description:
True when the error came from a thrown `Response` (`throw new Response(...)` or a 404 from the router).
Narrows the value so `.status`, `.statusText` and `.data` are available.

throw new Response().description:
Throw from a loader or action to render the nearest `ErrorBoundary` with a status.
Caught by `isRouteErrorResponse()`, unlike a plain `Error`.
